nodes.label: creational pattern
nodes.def: A design pattern category focused on object creation mechanisms, abstracting the instantiation process so that code remains independent of the specific classes being created or how

nodes.label: structural pattern
nodes.def: A design pattern category focused on composing classes and objects into larger structures, defining relationships between entities to build flexible and efficient hierarchies.

nodes.label: abstract factory pattern
nodes.def: Provides an interface for creating families of related objects without specifying their concrete classes, operating at the level of abstraction.

nodes.label: abstraction
nodes.def: Simplifying complex reality by modeling classes appropriate to the problem, hiding unnecessary details while exposing essential characteristics.

nodes.label: abstraction layer
nodes.def: Boundary that separates concerns and hides implementation complexity behind a simplified interface for consumers.

nodes.label: active object pattern
nodes.def: Decouples method execution from method invocation in its own thread of control.

nodes.label: actor model pattern
nodes.def: Encapsulates state and behavior in message-passing actors that communicate asynchronously, with each actor processing one message at a time.

nodes.label: bulkhead pattern
nodes.def: Isolates resources so that failure in one part of the system does not affect others.

nodes.label: circuit breaker pattern
nodes.def: Prevents cascading failures by failing fast when a service is unhealthy.

nodes.label: clean architecture
nodes.def: Layered architecture with independent frameworks and clear dependency rules pointing inward.

nodes.label: hexagonal architecture pattern
nodes.def: Ports_and_adapters architecture that separates core business logic from external concerns, with ports defining interfaces and adapters implementing them.

nodes.label: abstract factory
nodes.def: Provides an interface for creating families of related objects without specifying their concrete classes.

nodes.label: adapter pattern
nodes.def: Converts the interface of a class into another interface that clients expect.

nodes.label: aggregate root pattern
nodes.def: Defines a cluster of associated objects treated as a single unit for data changes, with the aggregate root controlling access to internal objects.

nodes.label: ambassador pattern
nodes.def: Places helper services alongside consumer services to offload common connectivity tasks like retries, circuit breaking, and monitoring.

nodes.label: anemic domain model anti pattern
nodes.def: Domain objects with no business logic, just data storage, with all behavior residing in service classes, breaking encapsulation.

nodes.label: anti corruption layer pattern
nodes.def: Introduces a translation layer between incompatible subsystems, protecting the domain model from being polluted by external system models.

nodes.label: api gateway pattern
nodes.def: Single entry point for all client requests to backend services.

nodes.label: application service pattern
nodes.def: Defines operations that client code uses to interact with the domain, orchestrating domain objects and coordinating application workflow.

nodes.label: arrange act assert
nodes.def: Testing pattern structuring test methods into setup execution and verification phases.

nodes.label: balking pattern
nodes.def: Only executes an action on an object when it is in a particular state, otherwise returns immediately without doing anything.

nodes.label: big ball of mud anti pattern
nodes.def: System with no discernible architecture where components are intertwined through unpredictable dependencies and undocumented couplings.

nodes.label: bridge pattern
nodes.def: Decouples an abstraction from its implementation so both can vary independently.

nodes.label: builder pattern
nodes.def: Separates the construction of a complex object from its representation.

nodes.label: callback hell anti pattern
nodes.def: Deeply nested callback functions in asynchronous code creating unreadable code with inverted control flow and error handling duplication.

nodes.label: chain of responsibility pattern
nodes.def: Avoids coupling the sender of a request to its receiver by giving multiple objects a chance to handle it.

nodes.label: clean architecture pattern
nodes.def: Organizes code into layers with strict dependency rules: inner layers know nothing about outer layers, dependencies point only inward.

nodes.label: composite pattern
nodes.def: Composes objects into tree structures to represent part-whole hierarchies.

nodes.label: decorator pattern
nodes.def: Attaches additional responsibilities to an object dynamically.

nodes.label: dependency injection pattern
nodes.def: Supplies dependencies to objects rather than having objects create their own dependencies, inversion_of_control applied to dependency management.

nodes.label: domain model
nodes.def: An object model of the domain that incorporates both behavior and data.

nodes.label: double checked locking pattern
nodes.def: Reduces contention for locks by checking the condition twice (before and inside the synchronized block) for lazy initialization.

nodes.label: event driven architecture pattern
nodes.def: Organizes system around the production, detection, and reaction to events, coupling event producers to consumers through an event bus.

nodes.label: facade pattern
nodes.def: Provides a simplified interface to a complex subsystem.

nodes.label: factory method pattern
nodes.def: Defines an interface for creating objects but lets subclasses decide which class to instantiate, deferring instantiation to child classes.

nodes.label: flyweight pattern
nodes.def: Uses sharing to support large numbers of fine-grained objects efficiently.

nodes.label: mediator pattern
nodes.def: Defines an object that encapsulates how a set of objects interact.

nodes.label: microservices pattern
nodes.def: Structures an application as a collection of loosely coupled services organized around business capabilities, each deployable independently.

nodes.label: module pattern
nodes.def: Groups related code into self-contained units with clear boundaries, organizing namespace and controlling visibility of internal elements.

nodes.label: object pool pattern
nodes.def: Maintains a pool of reusable objects that can be checked out when needed and returned when no longer required, avoiding allocation overhead.

nodes.label: prototype pattern
nodes.def: Creates new objects by copying an existing object known as the prototype.

nodes.label: proxy pattern
nodes.def: Provides a surrogate or placeholder for another object to control access to it.

nodes.label: repository pattern
nodes.def: Mediates between the domain and data mapping layers using a collection-like interface.

nodes.label: service layer
nodes.def: Defines the boundary between application logic and the outside world.

nodes.label: service locator pattern
nodes.def: Provides a central registry to locate and retrieve services by name, acting as a registry abstraction for dependency resolution.

nodes.label: sidecar pattern
nodes.def: Deploys helper components alongside the main application container to handle cross-cutting concerns like logging, monitoring, or proxying.

nodes.label: singleton pattern
nodes.def: Restricts instantiation of a class to one single instance throughout the application lifecycle, providing a global access point to that instance.

nodes.label: spaghetti code anti pattern
nodes.def: Code with tangled control flow and unclear structure where changes cascade unpredictably across unrelated modules.

nodes.label: unit of work pattern
nodes.def: Maintains a list of changes and coordinates the writing out of changes and concurrency.

nodes.label: code smell
nodes.def: Surface indication that usually corresponds to a deeper problem in the system, suggesting refactoring may improve design quality.

nodes.label: cohesion
nodes.def: Measure of how strongly related and focused the responsibilities of a single module are, high cohesion indicating good design.

nodes.label: command pattern
nodes.def: Encapsulates a request as an object thereby allowing parameterization and queuing of requests.

nodes.label: composition
nodes.def: Combining simple objects to build more complex ones, favoring has_a relationships over is_a for flexible runtime behavior.

nodes.label: composition over inheritance
nodes.def: Favors composing objects with desired behavior rather than inheriting from classes.

nodes.label: composition over inheritance principle
nodes.def: Favors composing objects to get new functionality over inheriting from a parent class, reducing tight coupling.

nodes.label: consequence in design pattern
nodes.def: The tradeoffs and impacts of applying a pattern, including benefits and liabilities that affect the design decision.

nodes.label: consistent hashing
nodes.def: Distributes data across nodes minimizing reorganization when nodes are added or removed.

nodes.label: context in design pattern
nodes.def: The situation or circumstances in which a pattern applies, defining when the pattern is a good solution choice.

nodes.label: coupling
nodes.def: Degree of interdependence between software modules, high coupling making changes difficult and low coupling enabling independent evolution.

nodes.label: cqrs pattern
nodes.def: Separates read and write operations into different models for different optimization paths.

nodes.label: currying
nodes.def: Transforming a function that takes multiple arguments into a sequence of functions each with one argument.

nodes.label: data transfer object
nodes.def: An object used to carry data between processes to reduce method call overhead.

nodes.label: dead letter queue
nodes.def: Captures messages that cannot be processed successfully for later analysis.

nodes.label: dead letter queue pattern
nodes.def: Captures messages that cannot be processed successfully, enabling investigation and reprocessing without losing failed messages.

nodes.label: defense in depth
nodes.def: Multiple layers of security controls providing redundancy if one fails.

nodes.label: delegation
nodes.def: Handing off a responsibility to another object rather than doing it directly, composition alternative to inheritance for code reuse.

nodes.label: dependency injection
nodes.def: A technique where dependencies are provided to a component rather than the component creating them.

nodes.label: dependency inversion principle
nodes.def: High-level modules should not depend on low-level modules both should depend on abstractions.

nodes.label: design smell
nodes.def: Architectural issues that indicate suboptimal design decisions, potentially leading to maintainability or extensibility problems.

nodes.label: divergent change anti pattern
nodes.def: Single class modified in different ways for different reasons, indicating it has more than one responsibility that changes independently.

nodes.label: domain event pattern
nodes.def: Captures notable occurrences in the domain that have significance and may trigger downstream effects through an event bus.

nodes.label: domain model pattern
nodes.def: Uses rich domain objects with business logic rather than anemic data structures, encapsulating behavior alongside state in the domain layer.

nodes.label: double checked locking
nodes.def: Reduces locking overhead by checking the condition both before and inside the lock.

nodes.label: dry principle
nodes.def: Every piece of knowledge should have a single authoritative representation in the system.

nodes.label: dto pattern
nodes.def: Data transfer object carries data between processes, reducing the number of method calls by bundling multiple parameters into one object.

nodes.label: duplicate code
nodes.def: Same or very similar code existing in multiple places violating the DRY principle.

nodes.label: eager load
nodes.def: Loads all related objects as part of a single query upfront.

nodes.label: encapsulation
nodes.def: Bundling data with methods that operate on that data, hiding internal state and exposing only necessary interfaces to external code.

nodes.label: entity pattern
nodes.def: Objects defined by a unique identity that persists over time, with lifecycle continuity even as attributes change.

nodes.label: event bus
nodes.def: Central component that allows publishing and subscribing to events system-wide.

nodes.label: event driven architecture
nodes.def: Architectural style where the flow of the program is determined by events like user actions.

nodes.label: event sourcing
nodes.def: Stores state changes as a sequence of events rather than current state.

nodes.label: event sourcing pattern
nodes.def: Stores state changes as a sequence of events rather than current state, enabling audit trail and reconstruction of historical states.

nodes.label: eventual consistency
nodes.def: Consistency model where updates propagate eventually but reads may see stale data.

nodes.label: factory method
nodes.def: Defines an interface for creating an object but lets subclasses decide which class to instantiate.

nodes.label: fake object
nodes.def: Simplified implementation that works but takes shortcuts not suitable for production.

nodes.label: fake object pattern
nodes.def: Provides working implementations with simplified logic unsuitable for production, like in-memory databases or in-memory service implementations.

nodes.label: feature envy
nodes.def: Anti-pattern where code uses more data from another class than its own.

nodes.label: function composition
nodes.def: Combining simple functions to build more complex behavior.

nodes.label: gateway pattern
nodes.def: Encapsulates access to an external system or resource behind a unified interface, abstracting away the complexity of external communication.

nodes.label: god object
nodes.def: Anti-pattern where a single class has too many responsibilities and knows too much.

nodes.label: god object anti pattern
nodes.def: Anti pattern where a single class controls too much functionality, violating single_responsibility_principle and creating maintenance nightmares.

nodes.label: gossip protocol
nodes.def: Disseminates state information across nodes in a distributed system via peer-to-peer communication.

nodes.label: graceful degradation
nodes.def: System continues operating with reduced functionality when components fail.

nodes.label: health check
nodes.def: Endpoint that reports the operational status of a service and its dependencies.

nodes.label: hexagonal architecture
nodes.def: Ports and adapters architecture that isolates the core business logic from external concerns.

nodes.label: high cohesion
nodes.def: Design principle where related elements are grouped together keeping focus within a component.

nodes.label: hollywood principle
nodes.def: Dont call us we'll call you principle where lower-level components hook into higher-level frameworks.

nodes.label: idempotency key pattern
nodes.def: Ensures operations can be safely retried by tagging requests with unique keys that allow the system to recognize and deduplicate duplicates.

nodes.label: identity map
nodes.def: Ensures each object is loaded only once by keeping a map of all loaded objects.

nodes.label: immutability
nodes.def: State that cannot be modified after creation, simplifying reasoning about code and enabling safe concurrency.

nodes.label: immutability pattern
nodes.def: Designing objects whose state cannot be modified after creation.

nodes.label: indirection
nodes.def: Introducing an intermediate layer to decouple components, enabling flexibility and substitution of implementations behind a stable interface.

nodes.label: information hiding
nodes.def: Hiding design decisions within a module from other modules, exposing only the interface necessary for interaction.

nodes.label: inheritance
nodes.def: Mechanism where a class derives properties and behavior from a parent class, establishing an is_a relationship between types.

nodes.label: interface
nodes.def: Contract specifying a set of methods that implementing types must provide, enabling polymorphism through behavioral specification.

nodes.label: interface segregation principle
nodes.def: Clients should not be forced to depend on interfaces they do not use.

nodes.label: interpreter pattern
nodes.def: Defines a representation for a grammar and a mechanism to interpret sentences in the language.

nodes.label: iterator pattern
nodes.def: Provides a way to access elements of a collection sequentially without exposing its structure.

nodes.label: jwt token
nodes.def: Self-contained JSON token that securely transmits claims between parties.

nodes.label: kiss principle
nodes.def: Systems work best when they are kept simple and unnecessary complexity is avoided.

nodes.label: law of demeter
nodes.def: Object method should only call methods on itself, its parameters, its created objects, and its direct component objects.

nodes.label: layered architecture
nodes.def: Organizes code into layers where each layer only depends on the layer directly below.

nodes.label: layered architecture pattern
nodes.def: Organizes code into horizontal layers where each layer has specific responsibilities, requests flow downward through successive layers.

nodes.label: lazy initialization
nodes.def: Delays the creation of an object until it is first accessed.

nodes.label: lazy load
nodes.def: Delays initialization of an object until it is actually needed.

nodes.label: leader election
nodes.def: Algorithm for selecting one node as the coordinator among distributed nodes.

nodes.label: liskov substitution principle
nodes.def: Objects of a superclass should be replaceable with objects of its subclasses.

nodes.label: load balancer
nodes.def: Distributes incoming traffic across multiple compute instances to ensure reliability.

nodes.label: long parameter list
nodes.def: Anti-pattern where methods require too many parameters indicating potential design issues.

nodes.label: loose coupling
nodes.def: Design principle minimizing dependencies between components to improve maintainability.

nodes.label: mapper pattern
nodes.def: Creates a separate mapper object to transfer data between objects, keeping domain objects and data representations independent.

nodes.label: marker interface
nodes.def: An empty interface used to add metadata or capabilities to a class.

nodes.label: marker interface pattern
nodes.def: Uses an empty interface to tag classes with metadata that frameworks inspect at runtime to apply behavior or configuration.

nodes.label: memento pattern
nodes.def: Captures and externalizes an object's internal state without violating encapsulation.

nodes.label: memoization pattern
nodes.def: Caching function results to avoid redundant expensive computations.

nodes.label: message chain
nodes.def: Anti-pattern where code repeatedly calls methods on the results of previous calls.

nodes.label: message queue
nodes.def: Stores messages until they are processed and removed by a consumer.

nodes.label: message router
nodes.def: Routes messages from producers to consumers based on rules or content.

nodes.label: microservices architecture
nodes.def: Structures an application as a collection of loosely coupled independently deployable services.

nodes.label: middle man
nodes.def: Anti-pattern where a class does nothing but delegate calls to another class.

nodes.label: mock object
nodes.def: Simulates real objects with controlled behavior for testing purposes.

nodes.label: mock object pattern
nodes.def: Verifies interactions between objects by asserting that expected method calls occurred with specified arguments during test execution.

nodes.label: monad pattern
nodes.def: Design pattern that sequences operations while handling side effects in a pure way.

nodes.label: monolith architecture
nodes.def: A single unified deployment unit where all concerns are tightly coupled.

nodes.label: multiton
nodes.def: Ensures a class has a limited number of instances identified by keys.

nodes.label: mutex pattern
nodes.def: Provides exclusive access to a shared resource by allowing only one thread to enter a critical section at a time.

nodes.label: mvc pattern
nodes.def: Separates application into Model (data), View (presentation), and Controller (input handling), facilitating separation of concerns in user interfaces.

nodes.label: mvvm pattern
nodes.def: Separates View (UI) from Model via a ViewModel that exposes data for binding, enabling two-way data binding in declarative UI frameworks.

nodes.label: null object pattern
nodes.def: Replaces null references with neutral do-nothing behavior objects.

nodes.label: oauth pattern
nodes.def: Authorization framework enabling third-party access without sharing credentials.

nodes.label: object pool
nodes.def: Maintains a pool of reusable objects to avoid costly allocation and deallocation.

nodes.label: observer pattern
nodes.def: Defines a one-to-many dependency so when one object changes state all dependents are notified.

nodes.label: onion architecture pattern
nodes.def: Layers code concentrically with domain at center, surrounded by application services, then infrastructure, enforcing dependency inversion toward core.

nodes.label: open closed principle
nodes.def: Software entities should be open for extension but closed for modification.

nodes.label: outbox pattern
nodes.def: Writes events to a database table as part of a transaction to ensure reliable delivery.

nodes.label: parallel inheritance anti pattern
nodes.def: Two parallel class hierarchies grow in lockstep, requiring a subclass in one whenever one is added in the other.

nodes.label: parameterized query
nodes.def: Separates SQL logic from data to prevent SQL injection attacks.

nodes.label: partial application
nodes.def: Fixing some arguments of a function to create a new function with fewer parameters.

nodes.label: pattern catalog
nodes.def: Documented collection of design patterns organized by category, providing reusable solutions to recurring problems.

nodes.label: pattern language
nodes.def: Systematic format for describing good design practices within a particular context, connecting patterns into a coherent whole.

nodes.label: pipeline architecture pattern
nodes.def: Chains processing stages where each stage receives input from the previous stage, processes it, and passes output to the next stage.

nodes.label: pluggable architecture pattern
nodes.def: Designs system to accept interchangeable components through well-defined extension points, enabling runtime replacement of implementations.

nodes.label: polymorphism
nodes.def: The ability of objects to be treated as instances of a parent type while executing type-specific behavior at runtime.

nodes.label: premature optimization
nodes.def: Anti-pattern of optimizing before having evidence that optimization is needed.

nodes.label: principle of least privilege
nodes.def: Users and components should only have access to the minimum resources needed.

nodes.label: private class data
nodes.def: Restricts accessor/mutator access by encapsulating data inside a private inner class.

nodes.label: problem in design pattern
nodes.def: The recurring problem that a pattern addresses, describing the forces and constraints that create the design challenge.

nodes.label: producer consumer
nodes.def: Concurrency pattern where producers generate work consumed by workers in parallel.

nodes.label: producer consumer pattern
nodes.def: Decouples producers that generate work from consumers that process it using a shared buffer or queue between them.

nodes.label: program to interface
nodes.def: Program using interfaces rather than implementations for better flexibility and decoupling.

nodes.label: publish subscribe
nodes.def: Messaging pattern where publishers broadcast messages without knowing the subscribers.

nodes.label: pure function
nodes.def: Function that produces no side effects and returns the same output for the same input.

nodes.label: rate limiting
nodes.def: Controls the rate of requests a client can make to prevent resource exhaustion.

nodes.label: read copy update pattern
nodes.def: Enables lock-free reads by maintaining multiple versions and cleaning up old versions only after no readers reference them.

nodes.label: reader writer lock
nodes.def: Allows concurrent reads but exclusive access for writes to a shared resource.

nodes.label: reader writer lock pattern
nodes.def: Allows concurrent read access while ensuring exclusive write access, optimizing for workloads with more reads than writes.

nodes.label: refactoring
nodes.def: Restructuring existing code without changing its external behavior to improve internal structure, readability, and maintainability.

nodes.label: retry pattern
nodes.def: Automatically retries failed operations with configurable backoff strategies.

nodes.label: saga coordination
nodes.def: Manages sagas using a central orchestrator that tells participants what to do.

nodes.label: saga pattern
nodes.def: Manages distributed transactions across multiple services using a sequence of local transactions.

nodes.label: scatter gather pattern
nodes.def: Broadcasts a request to multiple recipients and aggregates the responses, used for parallel processing and result consolidation.

nodes.label: scheduler pattern
nodes.def: Centralizes timing logic for periodic or delayed task execution, abstracting scheduling concerns from task execution logic.

nodes.label: semaphore pattern
nodes.def: Controls access to a shared resource with a counter, allowing up to N concurrent accesses where N is defined at initialization.

nodes.label: separation of concerns
nodes.def: Dividing program into distinct sections where each addresses a separate concern, reducing complexity and improving modularity.

nodes.label: service mesh pattern
nodes.def: Adds infrastructure layer for service-to-service communication, handling load balancing, service discovery, and security without application code.

nodes.label: shotgun surgery
nodes.def: Anti-pattern where one change requires updating many classes across the codebase.

nodes.label: shotgun surgery anti pattern
nodes.def: Single change requires modifying many classes scattered throughout the codebase, indicating poor cohesion and excessive coupling.

nodes.label: side effect
nodes.def: Modification of state outside the local environment like changing a global variable, writing to a file, or triggering network call.

nodes.label: single responsibility principle
nodes.def: A class should have only one reason to change.

nodes.label: singleton
nodes.def: Ensures a class has only one instance and provides a global point of access to it.

nodes.label: soa pattern
nodes.def: Service-oriented architecture structures system as reusable services communicating over a network via well-defined contracts, promoting reuse.

nodes.label: solid principles
nodes.def: Five principles (SRP, OCP, LSP, ISP, DIP) that guide object-oriented design toward maintainable and understandable code.

nodes.label: solution in design pattern
nodes.def: The abstract structure that solves the problem, describing relationships and responsibilities among components.

nodes.label: space based architecture pattern
nodes.def: Uses distributed memory and processing grid to achieve scalability, avoiding central database bottleneck through in-memory data grids.

nodes.label: spaghetti code
nodes.def: Anti-pattern characterized by tangled control flow and lack of structure.

nodes.label: spy object pattern
nodes.def: Records information about how it was called during testing, allowing verification of calls after execution completes.

nodes.label: state pattern
nodes.def: Allows an object to alter its behavior when its internal state changes.

nodes.label: strangler fig pattern
nodes.def: Increments replaces a monolithic system by routing requests to either old or new implementation based on feature flags, gradually migrating functionality.

nodes.label: strategy pattern
nodes.def: Defines a family of algorithms encapsulates each one and makes them interchangeable.

nodes.label: strong consistency
nodes.def: Consistency model where every read receives the most recent write.

nodes.label: stub object
nodes.def: Provides canned predefined responses to method calls during testing.

nodes.label: stub object pattern
nodes.def: Provides canned responses to method calls during testing, returning pre-programmed values without any logic computation.

nodes.label: tell dont ask
nodes.def: Encourages telling objects what to do rather than querying their state and making decisions.

nodes.label: tell dont ask principle
nodes.def: Objects should be commanded to perform operations rather than being queried for state and making decisions externally.

nodes.label: template method pattern
nodes.def: Defines the skeleton of an algorithm in a method deferring some steps to subclasses.

nodes.label: temporal coupling
nodes.def: When the behavior of one component depends on another being called first, creating ordering requirements that may not be obvious.

nodes.label: test double pattern
nodes.def: Generic term for any object that substitutes for a real dependency in testing, encompassing mocks stubs fakes and spies.

nodes.label: test doubles
nodes.def: Generic term for any object that substitutes for a real dependency in tests.

nodes.label: thread local storage
nodes.def: Provides each thread with its own instance of a variable.

nodes.label: thread pool pattern
nodes.def: Manages a pool of worker threads to execute tasks reducing thread creation overhead.

nodes.label: tight coupling
nodes.def: Strong dependency between modules making changes difficult and risky.

nodes.label: timeout pattern
nodes.def: Limits the time spent waiting for a response before considering an operation failed.

nodes.label: transaction script
nodes.def: Procedural approach organized around procedures that process business logic.

nodes.label: transaction script pattern
nodes.def: Organizes business logic in procedures that handle each request, appropriate for simple applications without complex domain logic.

nodes.label: two phase commit
nodes.def: Distributed transaction protocol with a prepare phase and a commit phase.

nodes.label: two phase commit pattern
nodes.def: Coordinates distributed transaction across participants using a prepare phase followed by a commit phase, ensuring all-or-nothing semantics.

nodes.label: value object pattern
nodes.def: Objects that are defined by their attributes rather than a unique identity, immutable and interchangeable if attributes match.

nodes.label: visitor pattern
nodes.def: Lets you define a new operation without changing the classes of the elements on which it operates.

nodes.label: yagni principle
nodes.def: Only implement features when they are actually needed not in anticipation of future needs.

nodes.label: zero trust
nodes.def: Security model that requires continuous verification regardless of network location.
